q.questionsNormal.0.text: You have been away for two weeks. Work trip, long flights, bad hotel coffee. You are standing outside your front door with your bags. The lights are on inside.
q.questionsNormal.0.a: You don't stop. You push the door open and call out to whoever is in there.
q.questionsNormal.0.b: You put your bags down for a second. Just a moment before it starts again.
q.questionsNormal.1.text: It is the last night before your close group of friends splits up. New cities, new jobs. You are all at a table together and it will not happen like this again.
q.questionsNormal.1.a: You move around the table. There is something you need to say to each person before the night is over.
q.questionsNormal.1.b: You stay where you are. There is one person here who needs to hear something from you, and you are already next to them.
q.questionsNormal.2.text: Your company is throwing a big end of year party. Open bar, loud music, people you half-know everywhere. You walk through the door.
q.questionsNormal.2.a: You walk straight into it. Find a drink, find someone to talk to. You have been looking forward to this.
q.questionsNormal.2.b: You grab a drink and find a good spot. You like knowing who is in the room before you start working it.
q.questionsNormal.3.text: You have been doing this commute for two years. Same road, same time. You have got your headphones in and forty minutes ahead of you.
q.questionsNormal.3.a: You call someone. You have forty minutes and nothing to do with them.
q.questionsNormal.3.b: You put something on and go somewhere in your own head. This is some of the only real quiet time you get.
q.questionsNormal.4.text: You get home and your flat is full of people. Friends, some you haven't seen in years. Someone got them all here without telling you.
q.questionsNormal.4.a: You drop your bag and ask who wants a drink.
q.questionsNormal.4.b: You ask what is going on before you take your coat off.
q.questionsNormal.5.text: You are three months into a long and difficult work project. The hours are long and the end is still far away.
q.questionsNormal.5.a: What keeps you going is the team. Seeing them every day, the group chat, the shared frustration. You run on other people.
q.questionsNormal.5.b: You do not need the team for this. It is the work itself. The problem you are inside, the thing you are trying to get right. That is what gets you out of bed.
q.questionsNormal.6.text: Your manager pulls you into the corridor before the team meeting. Tells you quietly that you got it. Then asks: do you want me to announce it in there, or keep it between us for now?
q.questionsNormal.6.a: You tell them to announce it. You want the room to know.
q.questionsNormal.6.b: You tell them to keep it quiet. You will tell people yourself, one at a time, when it feels right.
q.questionsNormal.7.text: You run into your neighbour in the car park. You have a bag of shopping and somewhere to be. They stop and say hello.
q.questionsNormal.7.a: You stop properly. How long has it been. You have a few minutes.
q.questionsNormal.7.b: You say hi, check in quickly, and keep moving. You will catch up properly another time.
q.questionsNormal.8.text: You are at the airport saying goodbye to someone you love. The gate is closing. You have said everything there is to say. They turn to go.
q.questionsNormal.8.a: You call after them. One more thing. There is always one more thing.
q.questionsNormal.8.b: You let them go. You watch until you cannot see them anymore and then you leave.
q.questionsNormal.9.text: A friend you haven't spoken to in a while pops into your head. No reason. You just thought of them.
q.questionsNormal.9.a: You call. You want to hear their voice.
q.questionsNormal.9.b: You send a quick text. Just so they know you were thinking of them.
q.questionsNormal.10.text: You have been in the new city for three days and a colleague invites you to a big social event tonight. You do not know anyone there. You are still getting your bearings.
q.questionsNormal.10.a: You go. Meeting people is exactly how you get your bearings.
q.questionsNormal.10.b: You pass. You are still settling in and you need your own space before you start filling it with other people.
q.questionsNormal.11.text: An old friend asks how you have been. It has been a long time. You have a lot to say.
q.questionsNormal.11.a: You start from the beginning and you do not leave anything out.
q.questionsNormal.11.b: You give them the short version. Something true and light. You will save the real story for when it is the right moment.
q.questionsNormal.12.text: You get a call with life-changing news. Good news. The kind you have been waiting for.
q.questionsNormal.12.a: You hang up and immediately call someone. You need to tell someone right now.
q.questionsNormal.12.b: You hang up and sit down. You need to be alone with it before you can say a word.
q.questionsNormal.13.text: The job offer abroad has a deadline of midnight. You have been thinking about it all day. Your phone is in your hand. The people who would be most affected are one call away.
q.questionsNormal.13.a: You call them. You cannot decide this without the people it touches.
q.questionsNormal.13.b: You put the phone down and make the decision alone. This one is yours.
q.questionsNormal.14.text: Someone close to you has had a very bad day. They are sitting on the couch and they have not said much.
q.questionsNormal.14.a: You move closer. You find small things to do. You keep the space between you warm.
q.questionsNormal.14.b: You sit down nearby and stay. You do not reach for anything. You are just there.
q.questionsNormal.15.text: Your friend group is doing a big birthday dinner for you. Someone stands up and starts a toast. They are asking if anyone else wants to say something.
q.questionsNormal.16.text: The project is in its final stretch and your section is done ahead of schedule. You can jump in where the team is struggling, in the thick of it, or use the time to go deeper into your own work.
q.questionsNormal.16.a: You jump in. You do your best work when you are in the middle of things.
q.questionsNormal.16.b: You go deeper into your own work. That is where you will actually contribute the most.
q.questionsNormal.17.text: It has been a hard week. You are drained. Friday evening, nothing planned.
q.questionsNormal.17.a: You call a friend. You need noise, warmth, somewhere else to be.
q.questionsNormal.17.b: You run a bath and close the door. You need to be alone before you are fit for anyone.
q.questionsNormal.18.text: It is a summer Saturday. You have no plans. A friend texts: we are all at the park, come down.
q.questionsNormal.18.a: You grab your jacket and go. That is exactly what a Saturday is for.
q.questionsNormal.18.b: You've been looking forward to this empty day all week. You tell them maybe later.
q.questionsNormal.19.text: A mutual friend has had a death in the family. You have not seen them in over a year. You could text. Or you could go.
q.questionsNormal.19.a: You go. News like this should not arrive without a face behind it.
q.questionsNormal.19.b: You send a message. What matters is that they know. The distance is not the point.
q.questionsNormal.20.text: You are at a dinner. To your right, people are debating something that could change how technology works in the next fifteen years. To your left, your good friend Jacob apparently did something last weekend that everyone is talking about.
q.questionsNormal.21.text: A six year old stops you and asks why the sky is blue. You are in the middle of something.
q.questionsNormal.21.a: Light bounces differently off the atmosphere. Blue scatters more than the rest.
q.questionsNormal.21.b: You ask them what colour they think it should be.
q.questionsNormal.22.text: You wake up in a hospital bed. No memory of how you got here. A nurse walks in.
q.questionsNormal.22.b: You look at your hands first.
q.questionsNormal.23.text: You are watching Breaking Bad with someone. The scene where Walt lets Jane choke and does nothing. They turn to you: why did he not just help her?
q.questionsNormal.23.a: He could not. She was going to destroy Jesse. Walt made a choice between two people he cared about.
q.questionsNormal.23.b: That is the moment he stopped being a man who makes mistakes. Everything after that is just who he became.
q.questionsNormal.24.text: You find a photo of yourself from ten years ago. Someone asks what you see.
q.questionsNormal.24.a: Younger. The clothes. Where it was taken. That specific year.
q.questionsNormal.24.b: Someone who did not know yet what was coming. You can read it in their face.
q.questionsNormal.25.text: You are in a foreign city. Your phone just died. You have no map, no language, no data.
q.questionsNormal.25.a: Find a landmark. Reorient from something you recognise.
q.questionsNormal.25.b: Pick a direction that feels right and start walking.
q.questionsNormal.26.text: You are in a bar. Two strangers at the end of the room are about to come to blows. It is going to happen in the next thirty seconds.
q.questionsNormal.26.a: You clock the exits, the bottles on the bar, who is between you and the door.
q.questionsNormal.26.b: You watch the one who has not spoken yet. He is the one you need to watch.
q.questionsNormal.27.text: Someone hands you a file on the person you are about to negotiate against. You have twenty minutes.
q.questionsNormal.27.a: You start from page one. Background, history, every deal they have made before this one.
q.questionsNormal.27.b: You skip to their losses. That is where the real information is.
q.questionsNormal.28.text: You get an hour with someone at the top of their field. One question to open with.
q.questionsNormal.28.a: How did you actually get here.
q.questionsNormal.28.b: Where do you think this is all going.
q.questionsNormal.29.text: Two people near you are arguing. One has better facts. One has a better point.
q.questionsNormal.30.text: You just won life-changing money. First thought.
q.questionsNormal.30.a: What needs sorting. Tax, accounts, who to call.
q.questionsNormal.30.b: What it means. That version of your life is over.
q.questionsNormal.31.text: You are the first one awake at base camp. Summit attempt in two hours.
q.questionsNormal.31.a: You check the gear and the conditions.
q.questionsNormal.31.b: You sit outside and look at the mountain.
q.questionsNormal.32.text: A colleague makes a strong argument. The room is convinced. You are not.
q.questionsNormal.32.b: You challenge the assumption underneath it.
q.questionsNormal.33.text: Someone pitches a big idea. The room wants to move fast. You are not sure yet.
q.questionsNormal.33.b: Is this the right thing to do.
q.questionsNormal.34.text: You are watching a documentary about something that happened forty years ago. Your friend asks why you are interested in it.
q.questionsNormal.34.b: It explains something happening right now.
q.questionsNormal.35.text: Someone asks if you believe in luck.
q.questionsNormal.35.b: No, but I believe in patterns.
q.questionsNormal.36.text: You walk into a house that has been empty for years. You are the first one through the door.
q.questionsNormal.36.b: You stand still for a moment before you touch anything.
q.questionsNormal.37.text: Someone just got back from a year living completely off-grid. You get to ask them one thing.
q.questionsNormal.37.a: What was the hardest part practically.
q.questionsNormal.37.b: Why did you actually do it.
q.questionsNormal.38.text: A major new scientific discovery is all over the news. Your friend asks what you think.
q.questionsNormal.39.text: You meet someone at a party who has an unusual job you have never heard of.
q.questionsNormal.39.a: What do you actually do day to day.
q.questionsNormal.39.b: How did you end up doing that.
q.questionsNormal.40.text: A city block is on fire. To your right: a building containing blueprints for a technology that would allow mankind to produce a hundred times more energy, ending poverty, enabling space travel, launching a new golden age. To your left: an apartment building where you heard a child screaming ten minutes ago. You have not heard anything since. You only have time for one.
q.questionsNormal.41.text: Two colleagues disagree about who deserves credit for a piece of work. Both have a case. You have been asked to weigh in.
q.questionsNormal.41.a: You ask for the timeline and the documentation. The truth is in there somewhere.
q.questionsNormal.41.b: You watch how each of them talks about it. The answer is already in how they behave.
q.questionsNormal.42.text: Someone asks you to make an exception to a policy for them. The policy exists for a reason. Their situation is genuinely difficult.
q.questionsNormal.42.a: You hold the line. The moment you bend it for one person you have made it meaningless for everyone.
q.questionsNormal.42.b: You make the exception. The policy exists to help people, and following it here would do the opposite.
q.questionsNormal.43.text: A colleague you are close to gets some very bad personal news during the working day. They are visibly struggling.
q.questionsNormal.43.a: You ask what they need. What is the next step.
q.questionsNormal.43.b: You sit with them. They need to know someone is there.
q.questionsNormal.44.text: You have to give someone feedback that is going to be hard to hear. Their work is not good enough.
q.questionsNormal.44.a: You say it plainly and without delay.
q.questionsNormal.44.b: You choose your moment and your words carefully.
q.questionsNormal.45.text: You are hiring for a role and you have two strong final candidates. One is more talented but works alone. The other is slightly less skilled but makes everyone around them better.
q.questionsNormal.45.a: You hire the first one. Talent is the whole point.
q.questionsNormal.45.b: You hire the second one. A team that cannot function together eventually stops working at all.
q.questionsNormal.46.text: A friend is about to make a decision you think they will regret. They have not asked for your opinion.
q.questionsNormal.46.a: You tell them what you think, clearly. A warning delivered too gently is not a warning at all.
q.questionsNormal.46.b: You find the right moment and the right words. A warning badly delivered gets dismissed.
q.questionsNormal.47.text: Two people on your team are in conflict. It has been going on for weeks and it is affecting the whole group.
q.questionsNormal.47.a: You sit them both down and tell them plainly what their problem is costing the team.
q.questionsNormal.47.b: You speak to each of them separately first. You want to understand what each of their perspectives.
q.questionsNormal.48.text: A project went well. Your manager asks who deserves the recognition. One person did most of the visible work. The other held the whole thing together quietly and nobody really noticed.
q.questionsNormal.48.a: You name the one with the visible output. Recognition should follow results, not invisible effort.
q.questionsNormal.48.b: You name the one who held it together. You were the only one who saw what it actually cost them.
q.questionsNormal.49.text: Someone who hurt you badly wants to make things right. They have changed. You can see it. The question is whether what they did is something you can move past.
q.questionsNormal.49.a: You can move forward, but the relationship is different now. What happened is part of the record.
q.questionsNormal.49.b: You let it go completely. Holding the ledger open is its own kind of damage.
q.questionsNormal.50.text: A project you are part of is clearly failing. Nobody has said it out loud yet. Your manager pulls you aside and asks what you honestly think.
q.questionsNormal.50.a: You tell them straight. The longer it stays unspoken, the more it costs everyone.
q.questionsNormal.50.b: You think about the people in the room first. How you say this matters as much as what you say.
q.questionsNormal.51.text: Your father needs expensive care. You have the money but it would wipe out what you set aside for your child's education.
q.questionsNormal.52.text: Your best friend's husband has been cheating on her. You have proof. She is three months pregnant and they just put an offer on a house.
q.questionsNormal.52.a: You tell her. She deserves to know.
q.questionsNormal.52.b: You say nothing. Not now. Not with everything she has ahead of her.
q.questionsNormal.53.text: A family member has left their estate unevenly. The person who got less was clearly there more. The will is legal and clear.
q.questionsNormal.53.a: You follow it as written. It was theirs to give as they chose.
q.questionsNormal.53.b: You find a way to make sure the person who got less knows their years were seen, even if the numbers do not show it.
q.questionsNormal.54.text: Your teenage son tells you he did something that could get another kid expelled. The other kid is innocent. Your son is terrified.
q.questionsNormal.54.a: You tell him to come forward.
q.questionsNormal.54.b: You tell him you will figure it out together.
q.questionsNormal.55.text: You are competing for something you want against someone you respect. You have a move that would probably work but that you are not proud of.
q.questionsNormal.55.a: You use it. Winning is the point.
q.questionsNormal.55.b: You do not use it. The cost is not worth it.
q.questionsNormal.56.text: Your best friend has been drinking heavily since the divorce. He is not talking about it.
q.questionsNormal.56.a: You wait for him to bring it up.
q.questionsNormal.57.text: Your company is being investigated. Your boss asks you to leave certain details out of your statement. He has been good to you for ten years.
q.questionsNormal.57.a: You tell the truth in full.
q.questionsNormal.57.b: You leave out what he asked you to leave out.
q.questionsNormal.58.text: The person you have been mentoring for two years has made a serious mistake in front of the team. Not careless. A real misunderstanding of something fundamental.
q.questionsNormal.58.a: You correct it plainly and in full, in front of the others. They will all face the same situation one day.
q.questionsNormal.58.b: You pull them aside. The lesson needs to land, not the audience.
q.questionsNormal.59.text: You are going on a road trip with a friend. No deadline, just the two of you.
q.questionsNormal.59.a: You plan the route before you go.
q.questionsNormal.59.b: You get in the car and figure it out as you go.
q.questionsNormal.60.text: You have a project due in three weeks. You have everything you need to start. More information might still come in.
q.questionsNormal.60.a: You start now. The worst thing is to need more time and not have it.
q.questionsNormal.60.b: You wait a few more days. Acting on incomplete information wastes the work.
q.questionsNormal.61.text: You are taking over a project halfway through. There are detailed notes from the previous person.
q.questionsNormal.61.a: You read everything before you touch anything. You need to understand what was intended.
q.questionsNormal.61.b: You start working and use the notes to answer questions as they come up. The best way to understand a plan is to work with it.
q.questionsNormal.62.text: You are hosting a dinner for eight people. It is three weeks away.
q.questionsNormal.62.a: You start planning today. A dinner this size does not come together on short notice.
q.questionsNormal.62.b: You know from experience that the best dinners have room to breathe. You will sort it closer to the time.
q.questionsNormal.63.text: You are in the middle of a disagreement that has been going on for an hour. You are not getting anywhere. You have somewhere else to be.
q.questionsNormal.63.a: You do not leave until it is resolved one way or another. You will not carry an open thing.
q.questionsNormal.63.b: You call it. This conversation is not going anywhere right now. You can come back to it.
q.questionsNormal.64.text: You have a free afternoon and you feel like going for a long walk. You do not have to be anywhere.
q.questionsNormal.64.a: You decide roughly where you are going before you leave.
q.questionsNormal.64.b: You pick a direction and go.
q.questionsNormal.65.text: You are told you have six months to live. The next morning you wake up.
q.questionsNormal.65.b: You call someone and ask if they want to go somewhere.
q.questionsNormal.66.text: You need to get somewhere and there is a route you have never taken before. It might be faster.
q.questionsNormal.66.a: You check it on the map first. You want to know what you are committing to before you turn off.
q.questionsNormal.66.b: You take it. You will know soon enough if it was the right call.
q.questionsNormal.67.text: You are starting a new hobby you know nothing about.
q.questionsNormal.67.a: You research it properly before you begin.
q.questionsNormal.67.b: You just start and learn as you go.
q.questionsNormal.68.text: You are going away for a week tomorrow.
q.questionsNormal.68.a: You pack everything tonight. Everything in the bag has a purpose.
q.questionsNormal.68.b: You pack in the morning. You know roughly what you need.
q.questionsNormal.69.text: Someone important just left your team. There is one internal candidate. They are not quite right.
q.questionsNormal.69.a: You hire them. The gap costs more every week.
q.questionsNormal.69.b: You wait for the right person.
q.questionsNormal.70.text: You have saved enough to either put a deposit on a flat or start the business you have been planning for three years. You have to decide by Friday.
q.questionsNormal.70.b: The business. You will regret it if you don't.
q.questionsNormal.71.text: You are three months into building a company. You just found out a major competitor launched the same product last week. You have a team of five waiting for direction.
q.questionsNormal.71.a: You stop and reassess before you make another move.
q.questionsNormal.71.b: You keep building. Stopping now is the only way to actually lose.
q.questionsNormal.72.text: Tomorrow you are switching off your parent's life support. The doctors say there is no chance. You are sitting in the hospital corridor tonight.
q.questionsNormal.72.a: You go back through all the medical reports one more time.
q.questionsNormal.72.b: You go home and sleep. You have already made the decision.
q.questionsNormal.73.text: You wake up in a hospital bed in a country you do not recognise. No ID. No phone. Nobody in the room.
q.questionsNormal.73.a: You stay put until someone comes and you can get information.
q.questionsNormal.73.b: You get up and start looking for answers.
q.questionsNormal.74.text: You just got out of prison after four years. First night of freedom. You have nowhere to be tomorrow.
q.questionsNormal.74.a: You plan the week. You are not wasting another day.
q.questionsNormal.74.b: You just sit outside for a while.
q.questionsNormal.75.text: You are halfway through a plan and someone suggests a genuinely better approach.
q.questionsNormal.75.a: You need a real reason before you abandon what was agreed. Changing for change's sake costs more than it saves.
q.questionsNormal.75.b: You hear them out. A better plan is a better plan, whatever was decided at the start.
q.questionsMyth.0.text: You have been gone for eight months. The campaign was long and ugly and you lost people you cared about. You are standing outside your house in Edoras. The candle in the window is still lit. You can hear your children inside.
q.questionsMyth.0.a: You push the door open. You have been waiting eight months for this and you are not waiting another second.
q.questionsMyth.0.b: You stand there for a moment. Your hand is on the door but you are not ready yet. You need just a breath before you become their father again.
q.questionsMyth.1.text: You are sitting at a long table with the people you love most, and the wine is good and the fire is warm and the night is slow. Somewhere in the back of your mind you know, though no one has said it, that this is the last time all of you will sit together like this.
q.questionsMyth.1.a: You move around the table, person to person. There is something you need to say to each of them before the night is over.
q.questionsMyth.1.b: You stay. There is one person here you came for, and you are already sitting next to them.
q.questionsMyth.2.text: You arrive in Pelargir on the morning of the midsummer market. The city is louder than anything you have heard in months, every street packed, music coming from three directions at once. You have until sundown and no obligations. A merchant you met on the road offers to show you around.
q.questionsMyth.2.a: You go with him. A city like this only gives itself up if you are inside it.
q.questionsMyth.2.b: You thank him and go alone. You want to find your own way through it.
q.questionsMyth.3.text: Three days of walking alone and on the second night you come across another traveller's camp. The fire is still going. They wave you over.
q.questionsMyth.3.a: You drop your pack and get into it. You ask where they are from, where they are going. Two days of silence and now there is a voice to talk to.
q.questionsMyth.3.b: You sit down and share the fire but you keep mostly to yourself. A nod and a few words. The company is enough without filling it.
q.questionsMyth.4.text: You come home and find the door already open, and inside there are strangers at your table and someone you know is laughing loudly, and the room smells of food and drink and other people.
q.questionsMyth.4.a: You drop your bag and ask who is hungry.
q.questionsMyth.4.b: You ask what is going on before you take your coat off.
q.questionsMyth.5.text: The war is over and the great hall of Dunmore has been thrown open. There is food and fire and music and people who have not laughed in months are laughing now. You have been sitting at the long table for an hour. Someone you fought beside leans over and asks if you are alright.
q.questionsMyth.5.a: You tell them you are better than alright. You want more wine and more noise and more of this.
q.questionsMyth.5.b: You tell them you are fine.
q.questionsMyth.6.text: Last night was the celebration. Today everyone is slow and quiet and the hall smells of cold food and burnt-out candles. You have a free day, no duties, nowhere to be. Someone knocks on your door and asks if you want company.
q.questionsMyth.6.a: You open it wide. Yesterday was good but today could be even better if the right people are in the room.
q.questionsMyth.7.text: You are crossing a wide plain and there are no landmarks and the road is empty in both directions, and then, far off, a lone traveller appears coming the other way.
q.questionsMyth.7.a: You stop. A conversation out here is worth more than it would be anywhere else.
q.questionsMyth.7.b: You exchange what is useful, water and distance and any warnings, and keep moving.
q.questionsMyth.8.text: Everyone you have been travelling with is going a different direction at the crossroads. There is still an hour before you all part ways.
q.questionsMyth.8.a: You make the most of it. You talk about everything that did not get talked about on the road. You want to leave nothing unsaid.
q.questionsMyth.8.b: You find yourself going quiet. The time that is left feels more important than filling it.
q.questionsMyth.9.text: You have been travelling under a false name for years. Tonight someone in the hall recognises you and says it aloud. The room goes quiet. The lord at the head of the table is looking at you.
q.questionsMyth.9.a: You stand up. If this is the moment, you meet it standing.
q.questionsMyth.9.b: You hold still. Being named is not the same as being ready. The room can wait.
q.questionsMyth.10.text: You have been stationed at the fortress of Helm's Deep for two months with a unit you did not choose. Tonight there is a fire in the yard and someone has produced a skin of wine and the off-duty soldiers are starting to gather. Your bunkmate leans out the door and tells you to come.
q.questionsMyth.10.a: You go. Two months and you still feel like a stranger in this unit. Tonight you fix that.
q.questionsMyth.10.b: You tell him to go ahead without you.
q.questionsMyth.11.text: You have been somewhere extraordinary and now you are back, and the people around you have gathered and they want to know everything and they are looking at you with open faces.
q.questionsMyth.11.a: You start from the beginning and you do not leave anything out.
q.questionsMyth.11.b: You give them something true and short, and save the real story for later.
q.questionsMyth.12.text: You have been given three days to decide whether to join the expedition to Rhûnost. It means two years away, real danger, and leaving behind everything you have built in Caldenmere. On the first night you are sitting at the table in your room with a candle and a blank page in front of you. Your friend Sera is downstairs.
q.questionsMyth.13.text: The physician in Drevath has just told you something about your health that you were not expecting. It is not a death sentence but it is serious and it changes things. You are walking back through the market alone. Your sister Mira is at home waiting to hear how it went.
q.questionsMyth.13.a: You go straight home. You need to say it out loud to someone before it becomes too heavy to carry.
q.questionsMyth.13.b: You walk for a while first. You are not ready to see her face when you tell her.
q.questionsMyth.14.text: Someone you love is falling apart, and they are not asking for help or solutions or answers. They just need someone there, in the room, close by.
q.questionsMyth.14.a: You move closer. You find small things to do. You keep the space between you warm.
q.questionsMyth.14.b: You sit down and stay. You do not reach for anything. You are just there, in the room with them.
q.questionsMyth.15.text: The war is over. The crown has just been placed on your head and the great hall is silent waiting for you to speak. Thousands of eyes. The people who bled for this are in the front row.
q.questionsMyth.15.a: You find your voice and you fill the hall. This moment belongs to all of them and you are going to make sure they know it.
q.questionsMyth.15.b: You keep it short. You say what needs to be said, you name the people who carried you here, and then you step down and go to them. The crown can wait.
q.questionsMyth.16.text: You are deep into a great project and your section is done. You can move to where the work needs you most, out in the middle of everything, or stay and push further into what you already know.
q.questionsMyth.16.a: You move. You want to be where the energy is, where things are still being figured out.
q.questionsMyth.16.b: You stay and go deeper. The work you do best happens when you are not being pulled in every direction.
q.questionsMyth.17.text: It is the third night of sitting with Rowan after his wife died. The others have started coming by again, filling the house with food and low voices and the kind of company that is meant to help. Rowan has not asked for any of it. He has not asked for anything. You are the one who has been here every night.
q.questionsMyth.17.a: You let them in. People need people and Rowan needs more than just you right now.
q.questionsMyth.17.b: You meet them at the door and tell them to come back in a few days. He is not ready and you know him well enough to know it.
q.questionsMyth.18.text: You have been travelling alone for three weeks through the hill country when you finally reach the waystation at Bree. There are six other travellers inside, a fire going, a meal on the table. The innkeeper asks if you are joining them.
q.questionsMyth.18.a: You pull up a chair before he finishes the sentence. Three weeks of nothing but your own thoughts and now there are voices.
q.questionsMyth.18.b: You take a room. You will eat alone tonight and feel human again in the morning.
q.questionsMyth.19.text: A message arrives that changes things. Not for you. For someone you know, someone you have not seen in a long time. You could pass it on and leave it at that. Or you could go yourself.
q.questionsMyth.19.a: You go. News like this should not arrive without a face behind it.
q.questionsMyth.19.b: You send word. What matters is that they know. The distance is not the point.
q.questionsMyth.20.text: It is the third morning of the harvest festival and you are on the hill above Caldenmere when you see it. A thin column of black smoke rising from somewhere past the mill road. The kind that comes from wet wood, or cloth, or something that was not meant to burn. Your brother is down there with his family.
q.questionsMyth.20.a: You run. You will know what it is when you get there.
q.questionsMyth.20.b: You watch it for a moment. The direction, the color, the way it is rising. Then you run.
q.questionsMyth.21.text: A man comes down from the mountain saying he has seen what is coming. Half the town is already moving on his word. He is standing in front of you and asking if you are with them.
q.questionsMyth.21.a: You ask him what exactly he saw. You will not move until the claim can bear some weight.
q.questionsMyth.21.b: You are already deciding. Something in what he said is true and you knew it before you could explain why.
q.questionsMyth.22.text: You ride into a village on the road ahead and find it emptied in a hurry. Fires still warm. Food left on tables. Whatever came through here did so fast and people ran. You have an hour before your company arrives and needs a report.
q.questionsMyth.22.a: You go building to building. You want to know exactly what happened here before you say anything.
q.questionsMyth.22.b: You already know what this means. You have seen this pattern before. You ride back to warn them now.
q.questionsMyth.23.text: You are two days into escorting a merchant through the Veldrath pass when you find the place where his last convoy stopped. The wagons are gone but the ground tells you things. Wheel ruts cut deep on the way in, shallow on the way out. Three sets of boot prints that do not match any of the convoy's crew. A child's shoe, half buried in the mud. The merchant is behind you asking what you see.
q.questionsMyth.23.a: You describe it to him exactly. The ruts, the prints, the shoe. He hired you to observe, not interpret.
q.questionsMyth.23.b: You turn around. You tell him the convoy left in a hurry, lighter than it arrived, and that someone who was not supposed to be there was. You do not mention the shoe yet.
q.questionsMyth.24.text: You have been travelling with Astrid for six days and she has been fine, steady, cheerful even. This morning she is quiet. Not tired-quiet. She ate nothing, she has not looked at you directly since dawn, and twice now she has stopped walking for no reason, just stopped, standing in the middle of the road staring at nothing. You are three hours from the border crossing and you need to know if she is going to make it through.
q.questionsMyth.25.text: You have found a written message in a language no one can read and you are told it may contain the directions you need. You have an hour. Two scholars offer different methods: one wants to map the patterns, one wants to feel out the meaning.
q.questionsMyth.25.a: You work on the patterns. Structure is the only reliable way in.
q.questionsMyth.25.b: You try to read it whole before breaking it apart. The feel of it will tell you more than the analysis.
q.questionsMyth.26.text: You are sitting next to one of the great masters of their craft at a long dinner, and you have their attention for the whole evening. What do you ask about?
q.questionsMyth.26.a: What the work actually looks like. The hours, the failures, the parts nobody talks about.
q.questionsMyth.26.b: Where they think it is all going. What everyone else is missing.
q.questionsMyth.27.text: A teacher finishes a story and asks the room what they took from it. The person next to you wants to know what you think before you give your answer to the group.
q.questionsMyth.27.a: You tell them what the story literally argues. You want to test the claim before you follow it anywhere.
q.questionsMyth.27.b: You tell them where the story took you. The literal meaning is not really the point.
q.questionsMyth.28.text: You are given one hour alone in a library so vast you could never read even a small part of it. You move through the shelves. You look for...
q.questionsMyth.28.a: Something specific. A subject you already care about, a question you have been carrying.
q.questionsMyth.28.b: Something you have never thought about before. You want to leave knowing something unexpected.
q.questionsMyth.29.text: Everyone has tried and failed and they are watching you approach. Before you reach for it you have a choice: test the stone to understand the mechanism, or simply try.
q.questionsMyth.29.a: You study it first. The angle of the blade, the gap, the material. There is a physical answer here.
q.questionsMyth.29.b: You reach for it without analysis. If it is meant to move it will move.
q.questionsMyth.30.text: The priest of Halvenmoor has been preaching the same sermon for thirty years. Tonight he gives it again, word for word, to a half-empty hall. Afterward your companion leans over and asks what you made of it.
q.questionsMyth.30.a: There are two claims in there that do not hold and you want to test them before you decide what to do with any of it.
q.questionsMyth.30.b: He was not talking about the gods. He has not been talking about the gods for a long time.
q.questionsMyth.31.text: A great speaker has just finished. The room is moved. On the walk back your companion asks what you made of it.
q.questionsMyth.31.a: You talk through the argument. There were two claims you want to test before you decide what to do with any of it.
q.questionsMyth.31.b: You tell them what it was really about. Underneath the words there was something else being said and that is the part that matters.
q.questionsMyth.32.text: The prisoner you were sent to execute was in his cell last night. This morning the cell is empty, the door is locked from the outside, and the two guards remember nothing. Half the garrison is already saying it was the gods. Your commander needs a report before noon.
q.questionsMyth.32.a: You document what you can verify. The locked door, the guards, the timeline. You will not write down what you cannot account for.
q.questionsMyth.32.b: You write that the man is gone and the how does not matter yet. Whatever this is, it is bigger than an escape and the garrison needs to be ready for what comes next.
q.questionsMyth.33.text: After months at sea your ship reaches land no one from your world has ever touched. The crew is ready to go ashore. Your second in command asks how you want to approach it.
q.questionsMyth.33.a: You go in and read it as you find it. What the ground is made of, what grows here, whether there is water. The land will tell you what it is.
q.questionsMyth.33.b: You tell him something feels wrong about the shoreline. Not the rocks or the trees. Something about the whole shape of it. You want to sail the coast before anyone lands.
q.questionsMyth.34.text: A raven arrives confirming that one of your oldest allies has signed a treaty with your enemy. On paper it is a trade agreement. Nothing in the letter is a direct threat. Your advisors say wait and watch. Something in you says this is not about trade.
q.questionsMyth.34.a: You wait. One letter is not a reason to act. You need more before you move.
q.questionsMyth.34.b: You start preparing. A move like this does not happen in isolation. Something larger is already in motion.
q.questionsMyth.35.text: You are the last scholar in a burned archive. One chest survived. Inside are two accounts of how the kingdom fell - the official record, detailed and cross-referenced, and a single letter from someone who was there, never meant to be found, that contradicts everything. You have one night before the chest is confiscated.
q.questionsMyth.35.a: You copy the official record. It is the most complete account that exists and preserving it is your job.
q.questionsMyth.35.b: You copy the letter. Anyone can reconstruct the official story. Whatever this letter is pointing at will not survive if you do not take it.
q.questionsMyth.36.text: You grew up in Annúminas and you have not been back in eleven years. The moment you ride through the gate you notice it. The market is where it always was but half the stalls are empty. The fountain in the square is dry. The people who do look at you look away quickly. Your contact is supposed to meet you at the inn by nightfall.
q.questionsMyth.36.a: You go to the inn and wait. You do not know enough yet to draw any conclusions.
q.questionsMyth.36.b: You already know something is badly wrong here. You go to the inn, but you sit facing the door.
q.questionsMyth.37.text: Two people stand before you and both claim the same child, and the child cannot speak for itself, and you are the one who must decide.
q.questionsMyth.37.a: You ask for the records. Birth, witnesses, dates. The truth is in there somewhere.
q.questionsMyth.37.b: You watch their faces when you say you will cut the child in two. The answer is already there.
q.questionsMyth.38.text: Your captain led you through three years of war and brought most of you home. Last month he was caught taking silver from the garrison fund. Not a lot. Enough to matter. The tribunal has asked you to speak at his hearing. You are the only one they will believe either way.
q.questionsMyth.38.a: You tell them what you know. The silver is the silver regardless of what came before it.
q.questionsMyth.38.b: You speak for the man. Three years of what he did for you has to count for something.
q.questionsMyth.39.text: A great elder collapses during a ceremony. They are alive but badly hurt, lying still on the ground in front of you. Everyone looks to you.
q.questionsMyth.39.a: You check the injury. You need to know what you are dealing with before anything else.
q.questionsMyth.39.b: You take their hand. They need to know someone is with them before anything else.
q.questionsMyth.40.text: The boy they caught stealing from the granary is fourteen. It is the third time this season. The law is clear, three strikes means losing a hand. The magistrate is away and they are looking at you to make the call. The boy's mother is in the back of the room. She has not made a sound.
q.questionsMyth.40.a: You apply the law. The third time is the third time regardless of who is standing in front of you.
q.questionsMyth.40.b: You send him home. Whatever the law says, you are not cutting off a fourteen year old's hand.
q.questionsMyth.41.text: You are responsible for two workers. One does work that is excellent and poisons every room they walk into. The other is average and everyone around them does better.
q.questionsMyth.41.a: You keep the first one. Results are the whole point.
q.questionsMyth.41.b: You keep the second one. A group that cannot work together eventually stops working at all.
q.questionsMyth.42.text: A man you respect is walking toward something that will destroy him, and he cannot see it, and you are the only one in a position to say something.
q.questionsMyth.42.a: You tell him plainly. A warning that is softened too much is not a warning at all.
q.questionsMyth.42.b: You find the right moment and the right words. A warning badly delivered is a warning ignored.
q.questionsMyth.43.text: Two elders of your community have argued badly and the group is split and the shared work is suffering and everyone is waiting for someone to do something.
q.questionsMyth.43.a: You go to both of them and tell them plainly what their argument is costing.
q.questionsMyth.43.b: You go to both of them and find out what each of them actually needs.
q.questionsMyth.44.text: The city is burning. You have done everything you can and you are at a crossroads. To the left is the last record of human knowledge. To the right is a street where someone may still be alive.
q.questionsMyth.44.a: You go left. The people had their chance and the record did not.
q.questionsMyth.44.b: You go right. You will not leave while there is still a chance.
q.questionsMyth.45.text: Someone who hurt you badly has come back. They have changed and they are sorry and they are standing in front of you waiting.
q.questionsMyth.45.a: You let them in. But opening the door is not the same as things being as they were.
q.questionsMyth.45.b: You let them in. The moment you saw their face you already knew you would.
q.questionsMyth.46.text: A great elder is dying and asks you honestly: how will history remember me? You know the answer and it is not simple.
q.questionsMyth.46.a: You tell them the truth. They asked for it and they have earned it.
q.questionsMyth.46.b: You tell them what was good and let the rest go. What purpose does the rest serve now.
q.questionsMyth.47.text: The ship is going down and there are two people in the water and you can only reach one of them. One is a healer who has saved hundreds. The other is someone you do not know.
q.questionsMyth.47.a: You reach for the healer. One life that saves hundreds is not the same as one life.
q.questionsMyth.47.b: You reach for the one closest to you. You cannot weigh a life in front of you against a number.
q.questionsMyth.48.text: The river broke its banks last night and the lower part of the town is flooded and underwater. You have enough boats to evacuate one street before dark. Narrow Lane is poorer, more people, harder to reach. The merchant quarter has fewer people but they are the ones who fund the garrison, the granary, the physicians. Your second is waiting for your call.
q.questionsMyth.48.a: You go to Narrow Lane. More people, more boats, that is the only math that matters.
q.questionsMyth.48.b: You go to the merchant quarter. Without what they provide, the town does not survive the winter anyway.
q.questionsMyth.49.text: A soldier comes home after a long war and everyone calls them a hero and there are feasts and celebrations and speeches. But you know something about what they did to survive.
q.questionsMyth.49.a: You say nothing. What they did to survive is between them and the war. It is over now.
q.questionsMyth.49.b: You find a quiet moment with them. Not to accuse. Just so they know someone knows, and still stayed.
q.questionsMyth.50.text: A woman in your village has accused a man of rape. He denies it. There are no witnesses. She is not the first to accuse him and everyone knows it, but knowing is not the same as proof. The elder has asked you to cast the deciding vote.
q.questionsMyth.50.a: You vote to wait. Without proof you cannot condemn a man, whatever your gut says.
q.questionsMyth.50.b: You vote against him. You have watched how people move around him for years. Some things do not need witnesses.
q.questionsMyth.51.text: A friend tells you they have done something wrong, something that hurt someone else, and no one else knows. They are not asking what to do. They just needed to tell someone.
q.questionsMyth.51.a: You tell them what you think they should do. Carrying it alone will not make it go away.
q.questionsMyth.51.b: You listen and you hold it with them. They told you because they needed someone to know, not because they needed a judge.
q.questionsMyth.52.text: Your enemy is on the ground and defeated and the battle is over and they are looking up at you.
q.questionsMyth.52.b: You lower your weapon and walk away.
q.questionsMyth.53.text: Someone close to you is carrying something heavy and has been for a long time. They have not asked for help and may not want it.
q.questionsMyth.53.a: You wait. If they wanted your help they would ask for it. Offering without being asked can feel like pressure.
q.questionsMyth.53.b: You find a way in. Not a direct challenge. Just a door left open so they know they are not alone.
q.questionsMyth.54.text: You are writing the history of a great war and you must decide how much of the human cost to include, and how honestly.
q.questionsMyth.54.a: You include what is true and necessary. The record must be honest or it means nothing.
q.questionsMyth.54.b: You include all of it. The people who suffered deserve to be in the story, not just the decisions.
q.questionsMyth.55.text: Your brother has been drinking again. You can smell it on him before he even sits down. He is supposed to testify tomorrow in front of the council on behalf of your family, and everything, the land, the debt, your mother's house, rides on how he presents himself. He does not know you know. He is looking at you across the table like everything is fine.
q.questionsMyth.55.a: You say it out loud. You tell him you can smell it and that he needs to hear what is at stake tomorrow.
q.questionsMyth.55.b: You say nothing tonight. Shaming him now will not sober him up and it will only make tomorrow worse.
q.questionsMyth.56.text: A great quest has been given to you and the road is long and the destination is clear but the way there is not known and no one has been before.
q.questionsMyth.56.a: You lay out what you know. The roads, the distances, the dangers. You want a shape before you move.
q.questionsMyth.56.b: You are already moving. The shape will come from the road itself.
q.questionsMyth.57.text: Word has come that a great flood is on its way and no one knows when. The sky is still clear and the ground is dry and there is no sign of it yet.
q.questionsMyth.57.a: You start building now. The worst thing is to need the structure and not have it ready.
q.questionsMyth.57.b: You watch the sky first. Acting too early on uncertain news wastes what you have.
q.questionsMyth.58.text: You have been asked to complete a great work that someone else began and left unfinished. The original vision is not fully clear and the person who started it is gone.
q.questionsMyth.58.a: You spend time understanding the original intent before you add a single thing. You will not build on a foundation you do not understand.
q.questionsMyth.58.b: You begin where they left off and let the work itself guide you. The best way to understand someone's vision is to continue it.
q.questionsMyth.59.text: You have been given charge of a great feast and kings and lords will come from across the land and it is many months away.
q.questionsMyth.59.a: You start organising today. A feast this size does not come together on short notice.
q.questionsMyth.59.b: You know from experience that the best feasts have room to breathe. You will pull it together closer to the time.
q.questionsMyth.60.text: You have been leading a long and difficult mediation between two communities and nothing has moved in weeks. Word arrives that someone who urgently needs you is somewhere else and the situation is serious.
q.questionsMyth.60.a: You do not leave until this is resolved one way or another. You will not carry an unfinished thing.
q.questionsMyth.60.b: You go. A mediation this stalled is already over. The real work is somewhere else.
q.questionsMyth.61.text: You are leaving at dawn on a journey that cannot be delayed. On the table is a letter that arrived last night. You have not had time to open it. You do not know what it says.
q.questionsMyth.61.a: You open it. You leave knowing.
q.questionsMyth.61.b: You pocket it unopened. You will read it when the road gives you a moment.
q.questionsMyth.62.text: You have travelled three days to attend a council of lords and when you arrive word comes that it has been cancelled and everyone is scattering.
q.questionsMyth.62.a: You feel the waste of it. The road, the preparation, the expectation, all of it for nothing.
q.questionsMyth.62.b: You look around at the people now standing with nowhere to be. You are here anyway. So are they.
q.questionsMyth.63.text: You are three days into a mission with a clear route. The bridge ahead is gone. There is no map for what comes next and the people waiting for you have no way of knowing why you are late.
q.questionsMyth.63.a: You stop and work out the best alternative before you move. A bad detour costs more than a short delay.
q.questionsMyth.63.b: You pick a direction and go. The road will give you options you cannot see from here.
q.questionsMyth.64.text: You are preparing for a long journey and you must decide what to bring and there is more you could take than you can carry.
q.questionsMyth.64.a: You make a list the night before and pack to it. Everything in the bag has a reason for being there.
q.questionsMyth.64.b: You pack the morning you leave. You know roughly what you need and you will sort the rest as you go.
q.questionsMyth.65.text: The kingdom has no leader and the council is divided and someone is filling the vacuum by acting as if they already hold the seat. They are asking you to back them publicly before a formal decision is made.
q.questionsMyth.65.a: You back them. The vacuum is the real danger. A decision now, even an imperfect one, is better than none.
q.questionsMyth.65.b: You refuse. Whoever takes this seat should do it properly or not at all.
q.questionsMyth.66.text: You were sent to hold the eastern gate. You held it. But while you were there, the enemy came through the western gate instead and your allies turned them back without you. The commander asks for your report.
q.questionsMyth.66.a: You report what you did. You held the post you were given and you held it well.
q.questionsMyth.66.b: You report what you missed. The eastern gate was never the real threat and you want to understand why you did not see it.
q.questionsMyth.67.text: You are halfway through building the garrison's winter stores when word comes that the regiment is being relocated in six weeks, not six months. Half the work you have done is now more than what is needed. Your crew is waiting.
q.questionsMyth.67.a: You finish what was planned. Stopping halfway leaves the work in a worse state than not starting.
q.questionsMyth.67.b: You cut the plan to fit the new timeline. There is no point building for a winter no one will spend here.
q.questionsMyth.68.text: Tomorrow is the reckoning - a trial, a ceremony, a choice that cannot be undone, something you have spent years preparing for. Tonight the preparation is finished and the fire is low.
q.questionsMyth.68.a: You go through it one more time in your head. You want to know every part of it before morning comes.
q.questionsMyth.68.b: You sleep. You have done what you can and the rest belongs to tomorrow.
q.questionsMyth.69.text: You arrive at the waystation where supplies were meant to be waiting. The building is empty. No note, no sign of what happened, just bare shelves. You have eleven people, two days of food, and four days of road ahead.
q.questionsMyth.69.a: You sit down and work out exactly what you have and what the options are before you move.
q.questionsMyth.69.b: You start walking. Standing still does not change what is in the pack.
q.questionsMyth.70.text: The work is done and someone is offering you two paths forward: take the next assignment now while the momentum is there, or take a month with no obligations before deciding anything.
q.questionsMyth.70.a: You take the next assignment. Momentum is harder to rebuild than to maintain.
q.questionsMyth.70.b: You take the month. You have not stopped in years and you do not yet know what you actually want next.
q.questionsMyth.71.text: You were sent to bring a man to trial. Three days of riding. A clear order. But when you get there, the man who was meant to oversee the arrest is about to kill him. No trial. No justice. Just an ending. You have seconds.
q.questionsMyth.71.a: You do nothing. The moment you go off-plan, you are the problem. Hold the line.
q.questionsMyth.71.b: You step in. The plan was made without this moment in mind. This moment changes it.
q.questionsMyth.72.text: Someone you love is dying and asked specifically for you to be with them at the end. You are in the room. Outside the door is someone they were estranged from for twenty years, who has just arrived.
q.questionsMyth.72.a: You stay. They asked for you. That has to mean something.
q.questionsMyth.72.b: You go to the door. Twenty years. Some things cannot wait.
q.questionsMyth.73.text: A child has been given the wrong medicine. Two options: one that works with certainty but causes permanent damage. One that may heal them fully but carries a real risk of death. The parents cannot be reached. The healers are divided. You must decide.
q.questionsMyth.73.a: You choose the certain option. The damage is real but the child lives.
q.questionsMyth.73.b: You choose the uncertain option. That chance is theirs to have.
q.questionsMyth.74.text: Your friend is about to confess to something he did not do, to protect someone else. The person he is protecting does not know. You are the only person in the room who knows the truth. He is about to speak.
q.questionsMyth.74.a: You stand. The truth is the only thing that matters here.
q.questionsMyth.74.b: You say nothing. This is his choice to make, not yours.
q.questionsMyth.75.text: You have been given the task of mapping unknown territory. You set out at dawn with your instruments.
q.questionsMyth.75.a: You work in a grid. Section by section, measurement by measurement.
q.questionsMyth.75.b: You walk until you find the highest point. The whole shape of it from above.
q.questionsMyth.76.text: Your ship can make it to the next port but only if you push through without stopping to fix the leak properly. A full repair here takes two days. The cargo is not urgent but the people waiting for it do not know that.
q.questionsMyth.76.a: You stop and fix it. Arriving late on a sound ship is better than arriving fast on a damaged one.
q.questionsMyth.76.b: You push through. The leak is manageable and two days here costs more than it saves.
q.questionsBoth.0.text: You've just arrived in Istanbul for a week-long work conference. Your flight landed an hour ago, check-in isn't until 3pm, and you have the morning free. You step outside the hotel.
q.questionsBoth.0.a: You pull up what you researched before the trip. You want to move with some bearings.
q.questionsBoth.0.b: You put the phone away and just walk. You pick a direction that feels right and let the city show you what it is.
q.questionsBoth.1.text: Your friend Marcus has just walked you through his plan to open a coffee shop in the empty unit next to his flat. He's been talking about it for months and he's finally ready to sign a lease. He asks what you think.
q.questionsBoth.1.a: You start working through the numbers in your head. Rent, footfall, margin on a flat white, how many covers he needs per day to break even.
q.questionsBoth.1.b: Something about the whole setup reminds you of two other places on that street that didn't last. You can't point to one specific reason yet but the pattern is familiar, and you tell Marcus to hold off on signing anything until he looks into it more.
q.questionsBoth.2.text: A recruiter calls about a senior role at Amazon. The salary is 40% higher than what you earn now, the work is exactly your skill set, and the team has a strong reputation internally. You also know Amazon was investigated three years ago over working conditions in its German fulfilment centres. Nothing illegal was proven but you read the reports at the time.
q.questionsBoth.2.a: You decline without interviewing. You don't want to spend your working hours building something for people whose decisions you don't respect.
q.questionsBoth.2.b: You go to the interview. A company this size has problems in every corner. You can do good work and be fairly paid without endorsing every decision made above you.
q.questionsBoth.3.text: Your friend group has turned on someone. Oscar dated someone in the group for two years, it ended badly, and now everyone is piling on in the group chat. You were close to Oscar and what they're saying doesn't match what you saw. No one is asking for your take.
q.questionsBoth.3.a: You go along with the general feeling. Your friend is hurting and keeping the group together matters more than your version of events.
q.questionsBoth.3.b: You say you saw things differently and that the full picture isn't being told. You know it will land badly but you can't put your name to something you don't believe.
q.questionsBoth.4.text: Your small business has had three bad months in a row. Revenue is down, a few clients have gone quiet, and your business partner wants to sit down and figure out what to do. You spend the evening before the meeting thinking it through.
q.questionsBoth.4.a: You go back through the numbers month by month. Which clients dropped off, what changed in each period, what you were doing differently when things were working. You want to understand exactly what shifted before you talk about fixing it.
q.questionsBoth.4.b: You don't need the breakdown. You already have a clear sense of where the business needs to go next and what it has been missing for a while. The meeting is about moving forward, not relitigating the last quarter.
q.questionsBoth.5.text: You have just been told your short film was rejected from the festival you most wanted to get into. You spent eight months making it. A friend immediately texts saying there are three other festivals with deadlines in the next two weeks and she can help you submit tonight.
q.questionsBoth.5.a: You say yes. The film exists, the work is done, and keeping it moving is better than sitting with the rejection.
q.questionsBoth.5.b: You tell her you're not ready to send it anywhere yet. You need to sit with it for a bit and decide if you even want to keep submitting, or if this one is just done.
q.questionsBoth.6.text: Your doctor calls on a Tuesday afternoon to say the test results came back and everything is fine. You had been quietly worried about it for three weeks without telling anyone. You hang up and sit in your car for a moment.
q.questionsBoth.6.a: You call your spouse straight away. You have been carrying this alone and now you want to share the relief with someone.
q.questionsBoth.6.b: You sit there for a while. Something about the three weeks you just lived through feels important and you want to understand what it taught you before the feeling disappears.
q.questionsBoth.7.text: You are at a house party and you walk into the kitchen to find your ex standing there. You haven't spoken in two years. The split was messy. They look up and see you at the same moment. The room has a few other people in it.
q.questionsBoth.7.a: You say hi and walk over. You are both here, it would be stranger to say nothing, and you can handle a five minute conversation.
q.questionsBoth.7.b: You give a small nod and find somewhere else to be. You are not ready to perform ease you don't feel.
q.questionsBoth.8.text: You are back in the town where you grew up for the first time in ten years. You have a free afternoon. Your childhood best friend Anton still lives there and has offered to show you around.
q.questionsBoth.8.a: You tell Anton you want to see what the place has become. The new parts, what's changed, what's moved in where the old things used to be.
q.questionsBoth.8.b: You ask Anton to take you to the places you actually remember. The school, the park, the route you used to walk. You want to feel what it was like, not see what it is now.
q.questionsBoth.9.text: You are clearing out your late grandmother's flat and find a shoebox under her bed. Inside is a bundle of letters tied with string, a handful of old coins, a photograph of a young man you don't recognise, and a ring you have never seen her wear. Your mother is in the next room.
q.questionsBoth.9.a: You look at each object carefully. The postmarks on the letters, the dates on the coins, the clothes the man in the photo is wearing. You want to piece together what this actually was.
q.questionsBoth.9.b: You sit with it for a moment before you do anything. Whatever was in this box mattered to her enough to keep it hidden, and that is the part that stays with you.
q.questionsBoth.10.text: You are at a two-day industry seminar. The sessions are decent but the most interesting thing happening is the conversations in the breaks. A colleague keeps pulling you into group discussions in the hallway. You also have a stack of notes from this morning that you want to think through properly.
q.questionsBoth.10.a: You stay in the hallway. The room is full of people who know things you don't and the conversations are where the real value is.
q.questionsBoth.10.b: You find a quiet corner with your notes. You need to actually process what you heard before taking in anything else.
q.questionsBoth.11.text: Your bathroom has needed renovating for two years and you finally have the money saved to do it. Then a group of friends announces a ten-day trip to Japan and sends you a link to split the cost. It would nearly wipe out what you saved. You have until Friday to decide.
q.questionsBoth.11.a: You send the money. The bathroom can wait another year. Japan with that group of people is not something you want to watch from home.
q.questionsBoth.11.b: You stay and do the renovation. You have been living with a broken shower and peeling tiles long enough and fixing your own space matters more to you than the trip.
type.ISTJ.name: The Inspector
type.ISTJ.description: You are the person who can actually be counted on. Where others talk about standards, you live by them. You approach life methodically gathering facts before acting, honouring commitments without fanfare, and finding deep satisfaction in work done properly. You have little patience for chaos or shortcuts, and you're often the quiet backbone of every institution you're part of.
type.ISFJ.name: The Protector
type.ISFJ.description: You notice what others miss the colleague who seems off today, the friend who's running on empty. You care deeply and show it through action: the favour done without being asked, the detail remembered months later. Loyal to a fault and disarmingly selfless, you are the person others instinctively lean on in hard times.
type.INFJ.name: The Counselor
type.INFJ.description: You are the rarest type and the hardest to read. You see patterns in people and situations long before anyone else does, and you hold onto ideals with a grip that surprises those who mistake your quietness for passivity. You're not just empathetic; you're strategic about it, investing deeply in the few rather than performing warmth for the many.
type.INTJ.name: The Architect
type.INTJ.description: You already have a better plan. You're not arrogant about it you just see structural flaws and inefficiencies that others walk past. You hold yourself to an impossible standard and find it genuinely difficult to respect those who don't hold themselves to any. Independence isn't a preference; it's a requirement. You build systems, visions, and long games.
type.ISTP.name: The Craftsman
type.ISTP.description: When things go wrong, you're the calmest person in the room and usually the most useful. You're a natural problem-solver who trusts what you can observe and test over theory and abstraction. You learn by doing, resist rules that don't make sense, and find most social performance deeply unnecessary. You respect competence above everything else.
type.ISFP.name: The Artist
type.ISFP.description: You live closer to your senses than most. The right music in the right moment genuinely moves you; beauty in unexpected places stops you short. You resist being put in boxes, defy categories quietly, and hold your values intensely while appearing flexible to the outside world. You give people space because you need it too.
type.INFP.name: The Mediator
type.INFP.description: You carry a rich inner world that most people never get to see. You feel the gap between how things are and how they should be more acutely than almost anyone, and that tension drives you toward art, toward advocacy, toward depth in everything you do. You give people the benefit of the doubt and believe fiercely in human potential.
type.INTP.name: The Thinker
type.INTP.description: Your mind doesn't switch off. You pull ideas apart to see how they work, find inconsistencies that others breeze past, and lose hours in rabbit holes that turn out to be more interesting than whatever you were supposed to be doing. You're not antisocial you're selective. The right conversation with the right person? You'll stay for hours.
type.ESTP.name: The Dynamo
type.ESTP.description: You read rooms the way other people read books fast, fluently, and with retention. You're perceptive about people, energised by action, and at your absolute best when you're improvising in real time. Plans are fine until they meet reality; you're better at handling reality than most. You make things happen by deciding and moving.
type.ESFP.name: The Performer
type.ESFP.description: You don't just enter a room you raise its temperature. You're genuinely interested in people, spontaneous in the best way, and you have a gift for making others feel seen and included. You are fully present in a way that's increasingly rare. Life isn't something to optimise; it's something to experience, and you do it more fully than most.
type.ENFP.name: The Champion
type.ENFP.description: You see potential everywhere in ideas, in people, in situations that others have written off. Your enthusiasm is genuine and contagious, and you make everyone around you feel like they're more interesting than they thought. Ideas come fast and often; follow-through is the harder discipline. At your best, there is no one more inspiring.
type.ENTP.name: The Visionary
type.ENTP.description: You enjoy a good argument the way other people enjoy good food it sharpens the mind, tests the idea, and reveals who can keep up. You're never just curious; you're sceptically curious, probing the weak point in every assumption. You're most alive when you're in uncharted territory, and you get bored at the same speed most people get comfortable.
type.ESTJ.name: The Director
type.ESTJ.description: You have a very clear picture of how things should work, and you're not shy about bringing them in line with that picture. You're organised, decisive, and you hold people to their commitments including yourself. Others can read this as demanding; you read it as basic respect for standards. You build structures that last because you build them properly.
type.ESFJ.name: The Caregiver
type.ESFJ.description: You are the connective tissue of every group you're part of. You remember birthdays, notice when something's off, and make sure no one is left out. You have a gift for creating the kind of warmth that makes people feel safe. Harmony isn't just nice to have for you it's something you actively work toward every single day.
type.ENFJ.name: The Teacher
type.ENFJ.description: You have a gift that's hard to explain you make people feel simultaneously fully seen and gently challenged to be more. You lead not through authority but through genuine belief in others. You're a natural at reading people and even better at inspiring them. The people in your life are often more capable than they were before they knew you.
type.ENTJ.name: The Commander
type.ENTJ.description: You see the destination before others see the problem. Your confidence isn't performance it comes from having already run the scenarios in your head and knowing which one wins. You lead because you can't stand watching things be done poorly when they could be done well. You are demanding, ambitious, and exactly the person you'd want on your side in a crisis.
